newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Disgraced South Korean ex-minister jailed.
newsitem.headline: Disgraced South Korean ex-minister jailed.

text.p: Disgraced former South Korean defence minister Lee Yang-ho was sentenced to four years in jail on Tuesday on charges of bribery and leaking military secrets, a court official said.

The verdict came a day after an appeals court upheld convictions on former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo for accepting kickbacks worth hundreds of millions of dollars and for other misdeeds.

Lee was sacked from the cabinet on October 17, ostensibly to shoulder responsibility for an embarrassing security lapse that allowed a North Korean submarine to slip in to Southern waters the previous month.
But it soon became apparent that military ineptitude was only the start of his problems.

Later in October he was arrested on charges of accepting 150 million won ($180,000) as his cut of payments to an arms merchant from Daewoo Heavy Industries in connection with the purchase of military helicopters.

Separately, he was charged with revealing details of purchases of sophisticated electronics to the Korean-American arms merchant, who vanished after turning up briefly in Beijing around the time of Lee's arrest.
Lee made a full confession and apologised during his trial for "stirring up trouble".
Prosecutors had demanded a six-year jail term.
The court also handed a two-year jail term, suspended for three years, to Sok Chin-chol, former president of Daewoo Heavy who now heads Daewoo Group's car subsidiary in Poland.
Chung Ho-shin, one-time vice president of Daewoo Heavy, was sentenced to 10 months in jail suspended for one year.
Daewoo has insisted the payments to the arms dealer were a commission, not a bribe.

The court also sentenced two employees of a company owned by the arms dealer, Lee Nam-hee and Kang Jong-ho, to jail terms of two years and 1-1/2 years, respectively, for extorting 50 million won from Daewoo.

Lee's disgrace damaged President Kim Young-sam by holding up to public ridicule Kim's campaign to clean up South Korean society and casting doubt on the military readiness of the country's much-vaunted armed forces.

Of 26 North Koreans who came ashore from the submarine, 24 were killed, one captured and one is still on the loose after a manhunt by 60,000 troops that was badly botched in places and resulted in several "friendly fire" deaths.
Adding to Kim's woes, health minister Lee Sung-ho stepped down last month amid bribery allegations involving his wife. Lee Sung-ho was cleared but his wife was arrested.

Daewoo also featured in Tuesday's appeals trial involving Chun and Roh when group chairman Kim Woo-choong's two-year jail term for bribing Roh was suspended for three years. At the same trial, Daewoo Corp chairman was Lee Kyung-hoon was cleared of a corruption conviction.

Chun's death sentence was commuted to life in jail and Roh's 22-1/2 year jail term was cut to 17 years. Both men were convicted of mutiny over a 1979 coup, treason over a 1980 army massacre in Kwangju and corruption.
President Kim has said the scandals in his cabinet will not slow his efforts to root out corrupt links between politics and big business.
The president has recently reshuffled the military top brass and ordered discipline tightened among rank and file to show the public he is acting firmly against the threat of any North Korean attack.
